rounds.text: Expo Engineering and Projects Ltd trades at an exorbitant valuation that is completely detached from its fundamental performance, highlighted by a towering P/E ratio of 143x and a price-to-book ratio of 4.77x [E1, E2]. This expensive pricing becomes even more indefensible when benchmarked against the broader sector, where the company's P/E of 105.26x and P/B of 4.64x vastly outstrip sector benchmarks of 26.76x and 2x respectively [E6, E7]. Operational metrics provide no support for these premiums, as demonstrated by a meager return on assets of just 2% compared to the sector benchmark of 7.08% [E8]. Top-line growth is deteriorating rapidly across every meaningful timeframe, featuring compounded sales growth of 4% over 10 years, -5% over 3 years, and a steep collapse of -44% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16, E17]. Furthermore, expectations have wildly detached from reality with price growth exceeding profit growth by 69%, while income-seeking investors receive no compensation given a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E57]. Conceded: the sector median sales growth is a robust 17.4%, yet the company's own 5-year compounded sales growth sits at a sluggish 7% alongside a flat mid-range position in its 52-week trading band [E5, E15, E74].
